title: workload sampler and cost-profile composer: automated defaults and safe rollout
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: We need a safer, higher-quality signal for automatic batching/caching and quantization defaults across diverse tenant workloads. Motivation: previous heuristics were brittle for tail-heavy SLAs and caused regressions in p99 latency for interactive endpoints (see ENG-7784). What this PR does: 1) Introduces a lightweight workload sampler that runs as an offline pass over request logs to produce a compact histogram of sequence lengths, token distributions, and prefix reuse signatures. 2) Adds a cost-profile composer that converts sampler outputs into candidate default profiles (batch-size ranges, cache TTL heuristics, and quantization-safe candidate list) with estimated per-token unit economics and a conservative safety score. 3) Builds a safe rollout path: composer produces profiles tagged with a confidence score and suggested canary parameters (percent traffic, latency budget overrides, monitoring probes). 4) Adds a new CLI (tools/econ/compose_profiles.py) and a small HTTP service (services/econ/composer_api.py) for integration into the Optimize pipeline. Implementation notes: sampler uses windowed sampling with reservoir sampling to bound memory; we persist signatures in a compact protobuf. Composer implements a small decision tree heuristic tuned on historical workloads and a fallback to global defaults when confidence < 0.35. Backwards compatibility: configs remain optional and old default logic is preserved behind a feature flag (econ.use_new_composer=false). Testing: unit tests for sampler and composer, integration smoke that generates candidate profiles for three representative workloads, and a canary simulation harness that evaluates estimated impact on token cost and latency. Rollout plan: initial staged rollout to internal customers first, then opt-in beta for existing Hosted users, automated monitoring with regression alerts tied to prompt sets. Related: ENG-7921 (cost-safety metrics), SUP-4123 (customer-reported odd batching behavior).

review_comments: Ravi Patel: Nice decomposition. Two asks: 1) can the sampler avoid touching S3 for small windows during dry runs? 2) add clearer failure modes to the composer (what happens if backend metrics are missing)?
Maya Chen (author): Answered - sampler now supports local log ingestion for dry runs and composer falls back to global defaults + emits a 'missing-metrics' debug tag.
Lena Ortiz: Please add a short performance benchmark for the composer service (qps at typical memory) and confirm protobuf backwards compatibility.
Maya Chen: Added a micro-benchmark in tools/econ/bench_composer.py and verified proto v1->v2 compatibility with a small adapter; included notes in docs.
Samir Khatri: request changes - tighten the confidence threshold for canaries and include a safety circuit breaker for p99 regressions in the rollout plan.
Maya Chen: Updated composer to annotate profiles with suggested canary thresholds and wired a circuit-breaker hook that triggers instant rollback when p99 delta > configured budget.
release_notes: Introduces a workload sampler and cost-profile composer to generate safer default batching/cache/quant profiles. Opt-in via feature flag econ.use_new_composer. Adds documentation and a canary simulation harness. Recommend monitoring p99 latency and cost deltas during rollout.
